subject.title: [Feature] Queue prompts when API limits prevent an immediate response

question: Should this issue become the canonical design tracker for a unified SQLite-backed capacity-wait prompt queue across provider exhaustion and followup replay?
rationale: The remaining behavior is not a mechanical bug fix: it requires choosing queue ownership, replay semantics, user-visible status, and how to coordinate overlapping open PRs.

options.title: Use this as canonical design tracker
options.body: Keep this issue open until a unified durable queue design lands, and require related PRs to align with that storage and replay boundary.

options.title: Split into narrower canonical PRs
options.body: Keep this issue open only as an umbrella while maintainers explicitly assign restart persistence, provider cooldown, and visible wait-state slices to separate canonical PRs.

options.title: Reject automatic replay for now
options.body: Close the direction only if maintainers intentionally decide current fallback/cooldown copy is the desired behavior and automatic replay is out of scope.

recommendation.title: Use this as canonical design tracker
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until a unified durable queue design lands, and require related PRs to align with that storage and replay boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent queue drain work and visible maintainer subscription make this the best available routing candidate for the cross-cutting queue/provider design choice.
